mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's shots FOR (all-prior and recent-5) alongside Team B's shots_on_target FOR (all-prior and recent-5), and cross with Team A's shots AGAINST and shots_on_target AGAINST (all-prior and recent-5). The mechanism is the joint ratio of shots-to-shots-on-target for Team B versus the corresponding ratio Team A typically allows, not either observable in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent shots volume rises sharply (recent-5 vs all-prior) while shots-on-target stays flat or declines, the on-target rate suppresses relative to raw shot volume; this divergence is amplified or dampened by Team A's own shots-allowed vs shots-on-target-allowed ratio, producing a joint interaction that rises or saturates non-linearly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume is structurally high relative to its shots-on-target conversion, and this ratio interacts with Team A's defensive shot-suppression profile: when a team generates many shots but a lower fraction on target, the joint relationship between total shots allowed and shots-on-target allowed for Team A determines whether Team B's volume translates into meaningful on-target pressure beyond what either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously — not a single observable mirrored against its opponent-allowed counterpart. The engine's covered class handles each observable independently; this mechanism is the cross-ratio interaction between the two.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's offsides FOR (all-prior vs recent-5 drift) and Team B's offsides AGAINST (all-prior vs recent-5 drift). The mechanism fires when both drift in the same direction simultaneously, indicating a shared structural shift in line-depth interaction rather than independent team-level changes.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's offsides FOR recent-5 is substantially below its all-prior mean AND Team B's offsides AGAINST recent-5 is also below its all-prior mean, the joint suppression of offsides is greater than the sum of the two independent suppressions — a non-additive interaction between attacking line depth and defensive line positioning.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offside rate FOR has collapsed in recent matches relative to its all-prior average, while Team B's offside rate AGAINST has also declined recently. The joint condition of both teams' offside observables moving in the same direction simultaneously — Team A running fewer offside traps or attacking lines and Team B conceding fewer offsides — suggests a structural interaction between Team A's attacking line depth and Team B's defensive line positioning that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single observable compared against its opponent-allowed mirror. It requires the joint drift of the same observable across both teams' perspectives simultaneously (Team A FOR drift × Team B AGAINST drift), which is a two-dimensional regime shift not reducible to one observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team B's corner_kicks FOR SECOND_HALF (all-prior) versus Team B's corner_kicks FOR FIRST_HALF (all-prior), and cross with Team A's corner_kicks AGAINST SECOND_HALF (all-prior) versus Team A's corner_kicks AGAINST FIRST_HALF (all-prior). The mechanism is the half-level asymmetry in corner dominance for both teams simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's corner production is more concentrated in the second half than the first half; Team A's corner concession is also more concentrated in the second half. When both half-level asymmetries align, the second-half corner imbalance between the teams rises beyond what the full-match averages would suggest, indicating a within-match state saturation effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner kick production is structurally higher than Team A's, and both teams show a within-match half-level asymmetry in corners (first half vs second half). The joint relationship between Team B's second-half corner dominance and Team A's second-half corner concession rate — both measured at half resolution — determines whether the corner imbalance is concentrated in the second half, which is a within-match state dependence not visible at full-match resolution.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires half-level resolution for both teams simultaneously and a joint comparison of first-half vs second-half splits across two teams — not a single observable at full-match level with one conditioning band. The within-match state dependence (half) combined with the cross-team joint condition makes this structurally richer.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's cards_2h FOR (second-half, all-prior) alongside Team B's yellow_cards FOR AWAY (all-prior) versus HOME (all-prior), and cross with Team A's cards_2h AGAINST (second-half, all-prior) and Team A's yellow_cards AGAINST (all-prior). The mechanism is the interaction between second-half card period and venue dimension for Team B, tested against Team A's second-half card-concession profile.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's second-half card rate is suppressed relative to its full-match away yellow card rate; when Team B plays away and the second-half period is isolated, the card accumulation for Team B rises toward its away yellow card baseline rather than its low cards_2h average — an asymmetric venue × half interaction that diverges from either observable's standalone level.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's cards_2h (second-half cards FOR) is substantially lower than Team A's cards_2h and the competition context, while Team B's yellow_cards FOR away is notably higher than at home. The asymmetric relationship between Team B's second-half card accumulation and its venue-conditioned yellow card rate — combined with Team A's second-half card concession rate — creates a two-dimensional conditioning structure: second-half period × venue, applied asymmetrically across the two teams' card observables.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (cards_2h and yellow_cards) jointly, conditioned on two dimensions simultaneously (second-half period AND venue), applied asymmetrically across the two teams. This is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's possession FOR (all-prior and recent-5) and Team A's fouls FOR (all-prior, recent-5, and venue split HOME vs AWAY). The mechanism tests whether Team A's foul rate co-varies with the degree of possession imbalance against them — a cross-observable joint relationship between two structurally distinct metrics across the two teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: As Team B's possession advantage over Team A grows (measured by the gap between Team B's possession FOR and Team A's possession FOR), Team A's foul rate rises — and this relationship is amplified when Team A plays at home (where their foul rate is lower on average) versus away, suggesting a threshold or saturation in foul response to possession pressure that differs by venue.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession dominance is structurally high (all-prior and recent-5), while Team A's fouls FOR away are elevated relative to home. The joint relationship between Team B's possession level and Team A's foul rate — where higher possession by Team B forces more defensive fouls from Team A — creates a cross-observable interaction: possession (Team B FOR) × fouls (Team A FOR), where the foul rate is expected to rise as a function of the possession imbalance, not independently of it.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and fouls) across the two teams, not a single observable mirrored. It also involves a threshold/saturation structure (foul response to possession imbalance) and a venue dimension interacting with the cross-observable relationship — three structural elements beyond the covered class.
